stories.headline: Calvin’s Take on Jacob’s Struggle: Divine Victory in Genesis
stories.summary: John Calvin reflects on Jacob’s night‑long wrestle with the divine, arguing that God’s presence turns conflict into triumph. He stresses that reliance on God provides defense against any opposition.

stories.headline: Original Sin: The Forgotten Pillar of America’s Founding
stories.summary: The article contends that the doctrine of original sin shaped the United States’ constitutional principles, yet many modern evangelicals now reject it. It calls for a renewed defense of the doctrine as foundational to American liberty.

stories.headline: Apple Vision Pro Brings Live Baseball to Immersive 3D
stories.summary: Apple will stream Friday Night Baseball in a new Vision Pro immersive mode, using 8K 180‑degree video for a stadium‑like experience. The debut game, Red Sox vs. Yankees, launches on August 28 for Vision Pro owners.

stories.headline: Needle2: A 14‑MB LLM Tailored for Edge Devices
stories.summary: Cactus releases Needle2, a compact language model built to run on smartphones, wearables, smart homes, and tiny robots. The update incorporates community feedback to improve tool‑calling and structured data extraction.

stories.headline: Mapping AI Knowledge Gaps: Claude and GPT Cutoff Insights
stories.summary: A deep‑dive examines how large language models like Claude and GPT handle information beyond their training windows. The analysis reveals timing discrepancies that affect factual accuracy and user expectations.

stories.headline: Ukrainian Drone Raid Deep Inside Russia Kills 13
stories.summary: A Ukrainian‑launched drone penetrated far into Russian territory, causing at least 13 deaths and injuring dozens more. Officials say the attack ranks among the deadliest since the invasion began.

stories.headline: WHO Alerts: Ebola Outpaces Control Efforts
stories.summary: The World Health Organization warns that rising Ebola cases are outpacing containment measures, signaling a worsening outbreak. Health authorities struggle to curb transmission as infection rates climb.

stories.headline: Russia Bars Sole Anti‑War Party from Election Ballot
stories.summary: A Moscow court has prohibited the country's only liberal, anti‑war party from participating in next month’s parliamentary vote. The ruling further narrows political opposition ahead of the elections.

stories.headline: Can AI Experience Emotion? A Talk with Rosalind Picard
stories.summary: Rosalind Picard joins host Christopher Watkin to explore whether artificial intelligence can sense and process feelings. The discussion examines the impact of affective computing on human well‑being.

stories.headline: AI‑Generated Writing: A Human‑Centric Call to Action
stories.summary: The piece argues that while technology isn’t opposed, humanity must retain intellectual autonomy against machine‑crafted content. It urges readers to safeguard critical thinking in the age of AI authorship.

stories.headline: Maverick Returns with Ferocious 'Almost Forever' EP
stories.summary: The surprise EP sees the proto-rage rapper channel his earlier intensity while adding fresh twists, avoiding a mere nostalgia act. It proves he's still a fierce contender in the underground.

stories.headline: New York Folk Singer Confronts Inertia on Sparse 'I Am Both'
stories.summary: The album strips back to skeletal arrangements, letting the artist's urgent lyrics blaze against personal and political stagnation. Its stark sound amplifies the call to action.

stories.headline: Apple's Chip Shortage Caps Earnings; Amazon's Results Under Scrutiny
stories.summary: Apple's latest quarter is throttled not by memory costs but by a shortage of chips, pressuring its stock. The piece then shifts to Amazon, dissecting Andy Jassy's market outlook and earnings performance.

stories.headline: Anthropic's Claude 5 Models Briefly Halted, Then Restored After Export Ban
stories.summary: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 were launched on June 9, 2026, but access was suspended on June 12 due to U.S. export controls. The ban lifted on June 30 and service resumed the next day.

stories.headline: July Marks Hottest Ocean Temperatures on Record
stories.summary: Global seas reached unprecedented warmth in July, spurred by a budding El Nino and ongoing wildfires across western Europe. The heat surge threatens marine ecosystems and intensifies climate risks.

stories.headline: NZ Guitarist and London Avant-Pop Star Fuse Into Ambient 'Nebular'
stories.summary: Veteran New Zealand guitarist teams with a rising London avant-pop vocalist to craft an album of hazy drones and wordless, celestial vocals. The collaboration feels like a seamless mind-meld, immersing listeners in a dreamy soundscape.

stories.headline: Trump's Gaza Proposal Faces Israeli Pushback, Yet U.S. Remains Unfazed
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu dismissed the Trump administration's 15-point Gaza plan, but Washington views the rebuff as political posturing ahead of elections. Officials expect negotiations to continue despite the public snub.

stories.headline: Apple Presses for Chinese Memory Chips Amid Global RAM Shortage
stories.summary: Reporting from San Francisco and Washington, the NYT and WSJ detail Apple's claim that chip scarcity drives price hikes and its lobbying for permission to source RAM from China. The move underscores the broader industry scramble for memory supplies.

stories.headline: Philadelphia Indie Singer Unveils Passion-Fueled Debut 'Chinook'
stories.summary: The songwriter's first full-length explores a lifetime of desire through varied styles, from tender ballads to soaring anthems. Its eclectic scope showcases a confident, emerging voice in indie rock.

stories.headline: Okanagan Wildfire Displaces Over 12,000, Leaves Homes in Ashes
stories.summary: A fast-moving blaze in Canada's Okanagan region forced more than twelve thousand residents to flee, with many discovering their houses destroyed. Survivors grapple with uncertainty as they await news on rebuilding.

stories.headline: Millions Defy War to Flock to Iraq for Shia Pilgrimage
stories.summary: Despite ongoing conflicts in the Middle East, over 20 million Shia pilgrims have gathered in Iraq for the Arbaeen festival, a testament to the enduring power of faith and community. The massive gathering has brought together people from across the region, defying the violence and instability that has plagued the area.

stories.headline: Stoa Markets Launches to Revolutionize Data Center Financing
stories.summary: Stoa Markets, a new platform, aims to disrupt the traditional financing model for data centers by providing a marketplace for new and used GPUs and AI servers. This innovative approach has the potential to democratize access to these critical resources, driving growth and innovation in the tech industry.

stories.headline: Assam Floods Claim 100 Lives, Displacing Thousands
stories.summary: Heavy monsoon rains have caused widespread flooding in India's Assam state, resulting in the deaths of over 100 people and leaving thousands without homes or livelihoods. The disaster has highlighted the devastating impact of climate change on vulnerable communities.

stories.headline: Introducing Ante: A Self-Sufficient Coding Agent
stories.summary: Ante is a revolutionary new tool that enables offline coding, providing developers with a secure and reliable way to work on projects without relying on internet connectivity. This innovative solution has the potential to transform the way we approach coding and software development.

stories.headline: Abuse Scandal Rocks Elite Art School, Iran's Midterm Impact
stories.summary: A shocking report has exposed decades of alleged abuse at a prestigious art school, shedding light on a dark secret that has been hidden for far too long. Meanwhile, Iran's ongoing negotiations have significant implications for the upcoming midterm elections, with the country playing a long game to shape the global agenda.

stories.headline: The Tragedy of the Cognitive Commons: A Warning for AI Researchers
stories.summary: A new study has highlighted the risks of the 'cognitive commons,' a concept that refers to the shared knowledge and expertise of the AI research community. As AI continues to advance at an exponential rate, researchers must be aware of the potential pitfalls and work together to mitigate them.

stories.headline: South African Special Forces Accused of Murdering Top Detective
stories.summary: A shocking investigation has uncovered evidence that South African special forces were involved in the murder of a top detective, sparking outrage and calls for justice. The case has raised serious questions about the country's security forces and their accountability.

stories.headline: Meta Returns to Open Models, Takes Aim at Closed AI Rivals
stories.summary: Mark Zuckerberg has announced that Meta is shifting back to open models, a move that is seen as a direct challenge to closed AI rivals. This strategic shift has significant implications for the future of AI development and the tech industry as a whole.

stories.headline: Illinois Passes Law Requiring Age Verification for Linux Users
stories.summary: A new law in Illinois has sparked controversy by requiring age verification for users of the Linux operating system, raising questions about censorship and freedom of choice. The move has significant implications for the tech industry and the open-source community.

stories.headline: Unlocking the Power of Rust SIMD on the GPU
stories.summary: A new article has explored the potential of Rust SIMD on the GPU, highlighting the benefits of this emerging technology for developers and researchers. By harnessing the power of parallel processing, Rust SIMD has the potential to transform the way we approach complex computations and data analysis.

stories.headline: Trump's Vaccine Order Blocked by Courts
stories.summary: President Trump's executive order to reduce the number of vaccines for children has been blocked by courts, despite his administration's efforts to change the vaccine schedule. The order has been met with resistance from health experts and lawmakers.

stories.headline: Silicon Valley's Billionaires Seek to Replace Democracy
stories.summary: A group of Silicon Valley billionaires and venture capitalists believe democracy is holding them back and are seeking to govern in its place, according to journalist Gil Durán. This 'unmasking' of their true politics has sparked concern about the influence of big tech on society.

stories.headline: Compressing Text Histories in SQLite
stories.summary: Researcher Simon Willison explores the idea of storing revision histories in relational databases by compressing text into a JSON array. This approach could provide a more efficient way to manage version control in databases.

stories.headline: Exploiting System Management Mode with a Long Interrupt
stories.summary: A researcher has discovered a vulnerability in System Management Mode that can be exploited using a very long interrupt. This finding has the potential to impact the security of systems that rely on this mode.

stories.headline: Trump Administration Recommends Splitting MMR Shots
stories.summary: The Trump administration has recommended separating the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine into three separate shots administered in different visits. This move has sparked debate about the safety and efficacy of the vaccine schedule.

stories.headline: Medicaid Rules Hinder Career Advancement for Disabled People
stories.summary: People with disabilities who work risk losing their Medicaid coverage if they earn too much, hindering their ability to advance their careers. New work requirements for Medicaid next year are expected to exacerbate this issue.

stories.headline: Former Thai MP Confesses to Murder on YouTube
stories.summary: A former Thai MP has confessed to shooting a government official on a YouTube livestream. The incident has raised concerns about the use of social media for confessions and the potential consequences of such actions.

stories.headline: OpenAI Calls for Responsible AI Infrastructure in Texas
stories.summary: OpenAI has written a letter to the Governor of Texas calling for responsible AI infrastructure in the state. The letter highlights the need for guidelines and regulations to ensure the safe development and deployment of AI technologies.

stories.headline: Practicing Hospitality in a Small Home
stories.summary: Living in a small home can make it challenging to practice hospitality, but it's not impossible. With a little creativity and intentionality, it's possible to create a welcoming space for guests despite limited square footage.

stories.headline: Gym Booking Website Vulnerability Exposed
stories.summary: A vulnerability in an Australian gym-booking website has been exposed, allowing users to cancel other people's reservations without authorization. This finding highlights the importance of robust security measures in online systems.

stories.headline: GitHub Models Shuts Down
stories.summary: GitHub Models has been retired, leaving users to find alternative solutions for their projects. The service was temporarily unavailable due to a scheduled retirement brownout.

stories.headline: Rekordbox Security Flaw Exposed
stories.summary: A vulnerability in Pioneer's Rekordbox has been discovered, putting users' data at risk. The issue has been acknowledged by the company, but details on a fix are scarce.

stories.headline: Reviving Handwriting Recognition
stories.summary: A 2016 project on handwriting recognition has resurfaced, showcasing the potential for AI-powered handwriting analysis. The technology has come a long way since its initial development.

stories.headline: Maine Senate Race Hinges on Women's Votes
stories.summary: In a competitive Maine Senate election, women's support is crucial for both candidates. Their votes could decide the outcome of the high-profile contest.

stories.headline: Crime Boss Daniel Kinahan Extradited to Ireland
stories.summary: Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan has been extradited from Dubai to Ireland, where he will face charges related to organized crime. His extradition marks a significant development in the investigation.

stories.headline: Daniel Kinahan Charged with Organized Crime
stories.summary: Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan has been charged with directing a criminal organization in Ireland. The charges follow his extradition from Dubai and mark a major milestone in the case.

stories.headline: Open-Source Alternative to Greptile
stories.summary: A new open-source project, Juror, aims to provide an alternative to Greptile. The tool is designed to offer a more accessible and customizable solution for users.

stories.headline: A La Carte: New Week, New Deals
stories.summary: The latest edition of A La Carte highlights Kindle deals for preachers and those who listen to sermons. A new book on happiness is also on sale, offering readers valuable insights.

stories.headline: Astrology App Store Rejection Story Retracted
stories.summary: A story about an astrology app being rejected from the App Store has been retracted due to inaccuracies. The retraction has sparked concerns about the App Review process.

stories.headline: Tupac Murder Trial After 30 Years
stories.summary: A former gang member will stand trial for Tupac's murder, a case that has gone unsolved for three decades. The trial marks a significant development in the investigation into the iconic rapper's death.
